security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, if the IOPMP's stall_violation_en CSR field (ERR_CFG[4]) is written via MMIO while the IOPMP programming state machine is in Steps 1-3 (i.e., MDSTALL.is_busy==1 or RRIDSCP write staging in-flight), and the hardware does not either (a) gate/block writes until is_busy deasserts, or (b) buffer the write and apply it atomically after Step 3, then in-flight DMA transactions checked concurrently may observe a mid-check change to stall_violation_en, causing transactions that should have been stalled-and-resumed to instead be faulted (dropped with no resume path), or transactions that should have been faulted to be stalled indefinitely. The spec explicitly declares this behavior undefined. Additionally, if the RTL hardwires mfr_en=1 in HWCFG2 while simultaneously hardwiring no_err_rec=1 in HWCFG0, software will attempt to use the multi-fault record (ERR_MFR) on an implementation without error capture capability, reading garbage/wrong values from the MFR scan FSM.
security_spec.summary: Spec declares stall_violation_en update during programming Steps 1-3 as undefined behavior and mandates mfr_en=0 when no_err_rec=1; RTL must gate ERR_CFG writes while is_busy=1 and cross-couple HWCFG0/HWCFG2 hardwired constants to prevent software from operating on non-existent error/MFR recording hardware
